newsitem.title: UK: East Midlands down as Dominion mulls offer.
newsitem.headline: East Midlands down as Dominion mulls offer.

text.p: Shares in East Midlands Electric were indicated 10p lower at 597-1/2 in pre-market trading on Thursday after Dominion Resources of the U.S. said late yesterday it would not pay more than 608p for the British power supply group.
Shares in East Midlands jumped 70p to 607-1/2p yesterday in rumour driven trading. After London markets closed, Dominion confirmed its interest in East Midlands.
But East Midlands on Thursday said it deemed an offer of 608p per share inadequate and would advise its shareholders to reject it.
Analysts agreed that an offer of 608p was too low.

"I'd say Dominion will be unsuccessful anywhere near six pounds. If you look at the precedent of other successful offers, you'd have to say that this one would have to come in north of eight pounds," said Greig Middleton analyst David Campbell.
"There are a lot of institutions that are loose holders of these (electricity) stocks, so maybe someone can get it cheaper, but they'd have to pay at least seven pounds," he added.
Nigel Hawkins, an analyst with Yamaichi, figures East Midlands would at least consider an offer of 650p. "They would and should look very closely at anything above 650p," he said.
